newsitem.title: PERU: Peru rebels allow first journalist inside building.
newsitem.headline: Peru rebels allow first journalist inside building.

text.p: Peruvian rebels holding 83 VIP hostages at the Japanese ambassador's residence in Lima allowed on Tuesday one journalist to enter the building for the first time since the early days of the siege.
The journalist went in shortly before 11 a.m. local time (1600 GMT) holding above his head a large sign which said "Kyodo," the name of a Japanese news agency.
A group of at least 10 other cameramen were allowed into the compound but did not pass into the building.
At a window above, hostage Gilberto Siura, a government party legislator, watched proceedings and waved at the journalists.

Tuesday marked the first day journalists had been allowed to approach the front of the building since the crisis began two weeks ago. A journalist helped Red Cross workers take in food on the first day of the drama.

The Tupac Amaru Revolutionary Movement (MRTA) rebels used the opportunity to shout an haranguing speech from within the building espousing their Marxist views and criticizing the government of President Alberto Fujimori.
